title: Generalizing Hate Speech Detection Using Multi-Task Learning: A Case Study of Political Public Figures
benchmark_measurement: Detection of hate speech directed at religious groups, with a specific focus on identifying Islamophobic content.
findings: The study found that Islam was one of the six primary topics for abusive and hateful speech from political figures. Muslims, along with immigrants, refugees, people of color, and women, were identified as the most vulnerable targets. The proposed Multi-Task Learning (MTL) model improved its ability to distinguish Islamophobic content after training, as shown by an increased clustering tendency for the 'Islam' topic in the embedding space. However, the model sometimes struggled to differentiate between general Islam-related content and Islamophobic hate speech, highlighting a key challenge in this area.
